summary: Wrote a 4-phase plan for the gate20 eager-load budget overage. Plan-time measurement found the dispatched premise stale: the eager total is 66707 B against a 66800 B baseline, gate20 passes 4/4 checks, and test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh passes 15/15 -- the overage was already closed by commit 9a43026d2 (2026-10-16) via a 381 B trim plus a documented baseline move 66100 -> 66800. The plan therefore implements route (a) as the task's goal prefers: confirm and record the current state, recover durable eager headroom by relocating duplicated eager content into existing non-eager homes, record the trim in the budget config with baseline_bytes left unmoved, then redeploy and run the full gate set. The two per-file ceiling margins (9 B and 3 B, both hard-mode fail) are flagged as an explicit non-goal and follow-up candidate.

artifacts.summary: 4-phase plan: evidence baseline and candidate audit, relocation trim to recover ~1500 B of eager headroom, dated config record with baseline unmoved, redeploy and full gate set.

decisions_made: Route (a) (trim) is the resolution this task implements; the already-recorded 66100 -> 66800 baseline move stands as a reviewed decision and is not reversed, since lowering a reviewed regression ceiling after a trim has no precedent in this config's own history.

Trimming the two per-file ceiling margins (commands/orchestrate.md 9 B, skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md 3 B) is excluded as an explicit non-goal: same noise class, different gate20 sub-check, two high-traffic files in concurrent orchestrate work's blast radius.

No user_decision raised: the verification-only-versus-trim fork is fully reversible file-edit scope, which the user-decision contract's own false-positive list assigns to the agent to decide and record.
